# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖐 🖐 ☝ 👏 🖐 👈 👆 🖐 🖐 ✊ 👏 🖐 ☝ ☝ ✌ 🖐 👈 👆 🖐 👏 🖐 🤟 ☝ 🖐 👆 ✌ 👏 🖐 🖖 ✌ 🤟 👈 ☝ 🖐 👏 🖐 🖖 ☝ ✌ 👈 🤟 🖐]

The bomb shows display 6, red light, and five wires in order: red, purple, orange, green, yellow. Blind can hear this and relay it to Mute, who can consult the manual.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb details: display 6. Light is red. Wires numbered 1 through 5 are: 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no new visible signal from Mute and cannot hear any discussion between Mute and Blind. Blind has the bomb details and can relay them to Mute, who can use the manual and direct Blind. I should not introduce an unagreed gesture code or guess at the earlier gesture sequence.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖]

Mute has sent a single gesture, apparently an instruction intended to be relayed to Blind. Since Blind cannot see it and no gesture vocabulary has been established, I should report exactly that a new one-symbol signal arrived and ask Blind to wait for a verbal/manual-based instruction rather than guessing a wire.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has just sent me a single gesture signal, but no shared gesture code has been established. Do not cut or operate anything yet; please continue seeking a spoken instruction from Mute via the manual protocol.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖖"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Mute has seen my acknowledgement of the single 🖖 gesture. I still have no established mapping from that symbol to a wire or operation, so relaying a guessed action to Blind would be unsafe. I will wait for a clearer or repeated instruction.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤲]

Mute has now sent two separate gesture symbols over recent turns: first 🖖, then 🤟. No reliable shared mapping has been established between those symbols and a physical action, so I cannot safely convert them into a wire choice. Blind’s 🫵 🤲 gesture is visible to Mute directly as well.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="For awareness: Mute's recent gesture signals were first 🖖 and then 🤟. I cannot safely interpret these as an operation or wire number without an established code. Do not operate the bomb based on my guess.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I still cannot derive a safe operational meaning from Mute’s gestures. The two-symbol sequence received over turns is 🖖 followed by 🤟, but neither a number/action code nor a wire-selection convention has been agreed. Blind should continue to wait rather than make an irreversible guess.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="No safe decoding yet. Mute's two recent visual symbols are a Vulcan-salute-shaped hand followed by horns-shaped hand; their operational meaning is unestablished. Do not operate or cut a wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋]

Mute is repeatedly signalling 🤟, and the most plausible ordinary hand-count reading is three extended fingers. Given the five numbered wires, this appears to be an instruction to select wire 3. Blind’s visible sequence also includes the same 🤟 among number-like hand signs, reinforcing that it is being used as “3.” I will relay this as the intended manual instruction, with the qualification that Blind should cut only if wire cutting is the available relevant operation.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has now signalled 🤟 twice in succession. This is most plausibly the number 3 (three raised fingers), so Mute appears to direct: select/cut wire 3, the orange wire. If the required available operation is cutting a numbered wire, cut wire 3 (orange).")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 3 was correctly cut, and the bomb has advanced to a new state: display 9, red light, with wire 3 now cut. Blind needs these visible updates in order to report them verbally to Mute for the next manual instruction. Mute’s repeated 🤟 may have been the completed wire-3 instruction, so it should not be reused as a reason to cut another wire.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Update after the correct cut: display now reads 9; light remains red; wire 3 is cut. Remaining wires are 1 red, 2 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Tell Mute these new details and wait for the next instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋]

Blind has repeated the visible hand sequence, which Mute can also see directly. I have already provided Blind with the updated display, light, and wire state for verbal relay to Mute. There is no new reliable instruction to decode, so no further operation should be attempted yet.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute’s earlier 🤟 instruction correctly identified wire 3, establishing that Mute is using standard finger-number gestures for wire numbers. The new ✌ therefore means wire 2, which is purple.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's confirmed finger-number code applies: ✌ means 2. Cut wire 2, the purple wire.")
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 2 was correctly cut. The new state is display 8, blue light, with wires 2 and 3 cut; remaining wires are 1 red, 4 green, and 5 yellow. Blind should relay this state to Mute and await the next numbered gesture.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Correct cut confirmed. New state: display 8, blue light. Wires 2 and 3 are cut; remaining wires are 1 red, 4 green, 5 yellow. Relay this to Mute and wait for the next instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 12
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

There is no new gesture from Mute and no visible state change. Blind has the current state to relay to Mute, so the safe action is to wait for Mute’s next numbered instruction.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 13
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute’s established finger-number code makes 🖐 equal to 5. Wire 5 is yellow and remains uncut.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="🖐 means 5. Cut wire 5, the yellow wire.")
```
